compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`bridge_status` (and the bridge last-pass detail reader) resolve the tracker as
`<repo_root>/.tickets-tracker`, hard-coded. They ignore the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` override and
the `tracker.dir` config key that every other read path honours, so on any deployment whose
tracker lives outside the repo tree the tool fails.

Observed 2026-08-27 against the LIVE MCP server
(`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`, container `compose-mcp-1`):

```
bridge_status {}
  -> Error executing tool bridge_status: {"error": "command_failed",
     "message": "cannot read bridge status: cannot read local environment id from
      /app/.tickets-tracker/.env-id: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
      '/app/.tickets-tracker/.env-id'", "exit_code": 1}
```

That path does not exist. The container's env sets
`REBAR_TRACKER_DIR=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`, and `docker exec compose-mcp-1 ls -a
/app/.tickets-tracker` returns `No such file or directory`. `fsck` on the same server reads the
env id fine (it reports `this environment ('eea68b7f-6697-488b-ac52-744e2ed8e96f')`), so the
env id IS readable — only this code path looks in the wrong place.

## Mechanism
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:89`

```python
path = repo_root / ".tickets-tracker" / ".env-id"
```

and the sibling constant at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:35`

```python
DETAIL_RELATIVE = Path(".tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/last-pass.json")
```

Both join the literal `.tickets-tracker` under the repo root. The caller
`src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:288` passes `root = Path(config.repo_root(repo_root))` and never the
resolved tracker. The correct resolver is
`rebar._engine_support.reads.tracker_dir()` (`src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:100-120`),
which returns the `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` override verbatim when set and otherwise joins the
configured `tracker.dir` name under the repo root.

## Impact
`bridge_status` is a read-only tool documented as always available. It is unconditionally
broken for every deployment using an out-of-tree tracker — which is the live server's own
configuration. The bridge freshness assertion (`max_age_seconds`) and the durable
last-pass/pause snapshot are therefore unreadable in production, and the error text
misleadingly points the operator at a path that is not the tracker.

## Reproduction
1. Set `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` to a tracker outside the repo root (as the deployed MCP server does).
2. Call `bridge_status` with no arguments.
3. Observe the failure naming `<repo_root>/.tickets-tracker/.env-id` instead of the configured tracker.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: `bridge_status` reads the env id from the tracker resolved by `reads.tracker_dir()`, so it succeeds when `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` points outside the repo root.
- [ ] AC2: `DETAIL_RELATIVE`'s last-pass detail file is likewise resolved under the configured tracker, not the hard-coded `.tickets-tracker` name.
- [ ] AC3: `bridge_status` also succeeds unchanged in the default in-tree layout (no `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR`, default `tracker.dir`).
- [ ] AC4: A regression test sets `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` to an out-of-tree tracker and asserts `bridge_status` returns a snapshot rather than raising.
- [ ] AC5: No remaining literal `".tickets-tracker"` join in `last_pass.py`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] DD1: AC1-AC3 hold, demonstrated by the AC4 test.
- [ ] DD2: `grep -n "\.tickets-tracker" src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py` returns no path-construction hit.
compiled_state.title: bridge_status hard-codes <repo_root>/.tickets-tracker and ignores REBAR_TRACKER_DIR, so it is broken for out-of-tree trackers
